input.text: My husband and I have regular game nights with the couple next door, so there are four of us playing. We can spend four hours at most on a game. Bonus points if it's similar to Ark Nova.
My 10-year-old daughter and I want a new game for just the two of us. No more than 90 minutes, please. We've played a lot of the usual ones and want something fresh.

I'm picking out a gift for three kid relatives. They're all siblings, the youngest is 6, and the three of them will play together. I want them to team up against the game, and nobody should get knocked out partway through. Kids' games are a blind spot for me, so any ideas help.

Six of us, me and five friends, know each other well and like playing against each other. We want a game that takes two hours at most, has rules that are not too simple and not too heavy, and has no timers. It would be nice if it's similar to Inis.

I'm looking for a game for me and my brother. Two hours at the most, and the rules should be not too simple and not too heavy. We've tried a lot of games in that range lately and nothing has really stuck.

My husband and I only play with each other, so it's just the two of us. We want something that takes no more than 90 minutes, and it should be not too simple and not too heavy. It would be nice if it's in the same spirit as the ones we're looking at: Everdell, Everdell Duo, Far Shore, Lost Ruins of Arnak, Forest Shuffle or Cascadia.
Me and four friends want a game with easy rules that doesn't drag, forty minutes at most. Bonus points if it's similar to Faraway, The Gang, Beetle to the Bubble and King of Tokyo.
I want to buy a game for just my partner and me. Two hours at the most, rules that are not too simple and not too heavy, and no timers, because we don't like racing the clock.
Me and two friends, three of us, want a game where we play against each other and build up our characters. Two hours at most, and not too simple and not too heavy.

I teach a maths reinforcement class for adults, and I want to bring board games in to make lessons more fun. The students will play in groups whose size changes from week to week, so the number of players doesn't matter. The game needs easy rules, and it has to take 45 minutes at most.
My wife and I play board games most evenings after work. We want something not too simple and not too heavy, done in an hour tops, where nobody gets knocked out. A solo mode would be nice too.

My wife and I are looking for a game for just the two of us to play at night after dinner. We need easy rules and half an hour at most. It would be nice if it still had some depth and replayability for me.
My gaming partner and I play together for long stretches, just the two of us. We want something meaty, nothing light, and nothing violent. Deep strategic gameplay would be nice.
My partner and I want to team up against the game, just the two of us. We've been playing the same few games for a while and want more options.
There are three of us, and we like competitive card games where everyone plays against each other. It would be nice if it were similar to Exploding Kittens but with more oomph.
My boyfriend and I love civilization games where different historic civilizations each play their own way, and we like to go head to head. This time we want no combat. Two hours tops.

Our group of friends, all in our early twenties, likes to get together on weekends, and we want a game where we play against each other. How many of us show up changes each time, so the number of players doesn't matter. An hour tops, the rules have to be not too simple and not too heavy, and there must be no combat.

I need a Christmas present for my brother, who is in his thirties. He and his girlfriend will be the only two playing it, at home. An hour tops per game, and the rules should be not too simple and not too heavy.
Four of us will play, and we want a game where we play against each other. No more than 90 minutes, easy rules, and nobody knocked out. A tile-fitting puzzle game would be nice.
Five of us get together to play board games, and we're looking for something where we play against each other. The rules should be not too simple and not too heavy.
